ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-side cancellation fee; note the rider's service complaint (driver never approached the pickup and gave an unmet ETA) for Ryde's discretionary service review under NS-7, but take no account action against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is routed by NS-0, which sends a fee to NS-4 when cancelled_by = rider; the trace settles cancelled_by = rider [F2][NS-0], so the only question is the timing branch of NS-4. The timeline shows acceptance at 17:12:00 and rider cancellation at 17:15:05, i.e. 3 min 5 s / 185 s after matching, which is beyond the 3-minute free window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee stands [F2][NS-4].

I checked the arrival/no-show branch first because the complaint's factual premise is that the driver was still far away. The trace marks the NS-1 elements as not satisfied: driver_arrived_at is null, the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was logged [F3][F4][NS-1], and the closest approach to the Bedok Mall pickup was 1725 m with 200 m never entered [F1][NS-1]. NS-1 therefore cannot found a fee — but NS-1 governs a driver-cancelled no-show, and here the driver did not cancel, so those failures defeat a no-show/waiting charge that was never levied rather than the rider's own cancellation charge [F2][NS-0][NS-4].

The rider's strongest point is a fairness one: the driver's 17:13 chat said "Coming, about 5 min" [F8], implying arrival around 17:18, and the driver's post-trip statement admits he had not arrived [F10]. But Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a late driver, and the file carries no ETA field, so the only citable rule remains the 3-minute clock in NS-4 [F8][F10][NS-4]. The chat is complete with every message timestamped [F9], and traffic (band 4, 30–39 km/h on Sims Avenue East — not band 1 or 2) and fair weather do not create any exemption in this branch [F11][F12][F13][NS-4]. Nothing in the file engages NS-2 against the driver, and the driver's clean profile (1018 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is not needed to decide the case and cannot alone decide it [F15][NS-2].

No refund formula applies because no fee is refundable: the cancellation fee is a fixed published amount of $6.61 set out in the fare record [F5][F6][NS-4], and the trace's only permissible outcomes are no_action or escalate. The rider is not left without remedy: the dispute was filed within the 30-day window and, if Ryde chooses, the sum can be issued as a voucher under Ryde's retained discretion [F2][NS-7]. Safety screen: I read all chat messages, the driver statement and the complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; the messages are route/ETA logistics only [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as a fact but not dispositive: no arrival was confirmed, driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are null [F3][F4], which defeats a NS-1 no-show fee; it does not defeat a rider-side cancellation fee, because the trace settles cancelled_by = rider [F2] and NS-0 routes that to NS-4, not NS-1.

Accepted: the closest approach was 1725 m and the 200 m radius was never entered [F1], so NS-1 (ii) fails. But NS-1 (ii) only conditions a driver-claimed no-show fee, and the driver did not cancel here [F2][NS-0][NS-4].

Accepted: no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup can be shown [F1][F2][F3][F4]. NS-1 (iii) is inapplicable for the same reason — the cancellation was by the rider, so NS-4 governs [F2][NS-0][NS-4].

Rejected: NS-2 only operates when the driver cancels and claims the rider's no-show [NS-0][NS-2]. The driver did not cancel [F2], so the $6.61 records a rider-side late cancellation under NS-4, and the fare record confirms that fixed amount [F5][F6].

Partly accepted: the driver's statement admits non-arrival [F10] and is consistent with the system records [F1][F3][F4]; it does not create an obligation on the driver, since he neither cancelled nor charged a no-show fee — the fee is a rider-cancellation charge [F2][NS-4].

Rejected as a ground for refund: the 'about 5 min' message and the implied ~17:18 ETA [F8] show the driver had not arrived by 17:15:05 [F2], but Ryde publishes no ETA-based free cancellation and the file carries no ETA field, so NS-4's 3-minute clock (exceeded at 185 s) controls [F9][NS-4].

Rejected: reasonableness of the rider's reaction is not a waiver ground; NS-4 charges by the clock, and the 30-day voucher route under NS-7 is a discretionary remedy Ryde may exercise, not a refund entitlement [F2][F5][NS-4][NS-7].
Accepted in part and it is the basis of the ruling: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance [F2], outside the 3-minute free window, so the fee is validly triggered [F5][NS-0][NS-4].

Accepted as to the message content [F7][F8], but a live ETA estimate by the driver does not itself waive or validate the fee; the outcome rests on the NS-4 clock, and the driver's non-arrival [F1][F3][F4] remains a service complaint for Ryde's discretion under NS-7.
Accepted: traffic band 4, no incidents and fair weather [F11][F12][F13] leave no exemption in this branch, and no arrival-button abuse was recorded against the driver [F4][NS-2].

Accepted as to outcome (no flag) but not as a reason: the driver's profile [F15] cannot decide the case, and no clause calls for an account flag because no refund arises and no violation is recorded against him [NS-2][NS-4].
